identification.summary: UAC-0094 is a CERT-UA-style uncategorized cluster identifier that Ukrainian authorities (the State Service of Special Communication and Information Protection, SSSCIP, and CERT-UA) used in April 2022 for activity aimed at taking over Telegram user accounts [S1][S2]. Malpedia lists the actor with no associated malware families [S3].
identification.notes: No Microsoft name or MITRE group was found. UAC-0094 is distinct from other UAC-numbered clusters such as UAC-0098 and UAC-0194 and should not be merged with them. Malpedia cites CERT-UA advisory #4360 (April 2022) as the primary document [S3].

attribution.confidence: Ukrainian authorities label the activity as a threat cluster, UAC-0094. Sources found do not state a sponsor or state nexus [S1][S2].
attribution.basis: SSSCIP and CERT-UA tracking of the Telegram phishing campaign, as relayed by press coverage [S1][S2]. The reference to Russia in the lure text is a fake login location, not an attribution finding [S1].

objectives: Unauthorized access to users' Telegram accounts by capturing the SMS one-time code; reporting describes the attackers obtaining session data, contact lists and message history once an account is taken over [S1][S2]. Strategic purpose is not stated in the sources gathered.

regions: Ukraine (Ukrainian authorities issued the warning to Ukrainian users) [S1][S2]
targeting.notes: Targets are Telegram users generally; no sector focus is stated in the sources gathered [S1][S2].

capabilities.summary: Social engineering through Telegram messages saying a login was detected from a new device located in Russia, with a link to a phishing page that collects the phone number and SMS one-time code to hijack the account [S1][S2]. Malpedia lists no malware families for this actor [S3].

campaigns.name: Telegram account takeover phishing wave
campaigns.summary: SSSCIP and CERT-UA warned of Telegram messages with malicious links, alleging a login from a new device in Russia, designed to harvest phone numbers and SMS codes and take over accounts. The activity was attributed to cluster UAC-0094 [S1][S2].

diamond.adversary: Unattributed cluster UAC-0094 as named by Ukrainian authorities; sponsor not stated [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Phishing via Telegram messages and a credential/OTP harvesting page; no malware listed [S1][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: A phishing domain imitating Telegram that requests phone number and SMS code [S1]. Specific domains were not captured.
diamond.technology: Telegram accounts protected by SMS one-time codes, which are exposed to real-time phishing [S1].

gaps: Could not open the primary CERT-UA advisories (cert.gov.ua/article/39253, listed in the record, and advisory #4360 cited by Malpedia); the profile relies on press coverage of them.
No sponsor or origin is supported in the sources found. The record's country value of RU is not backed by any source gathered; the Russia reference in the lure is a fake login location.
No activity after April 2022 was found.
Infrastructure indicators (domains, IPs) and victim counts are not captured.

Press coverage noted similarities to an earlier phishing attack using compromised email accounts of Indian organizations to hijack Ukr.net accounts; whether the same actor is involved is unverified [S1].
Implications left blank: sources are too thin for a JIPOE or JCC2 assessment.
